### 3. Workaround: implement your own parallel batch runner

Until you can upgrade to a version where the dispatcher-based `arun_many` is verified to work, you can do concurrent crawling yourself with `asyncio`:

```python
import asyncio
from crawl4ai import AsyncWebCrawler, BrowserConfig, CrawlerRunConfig, CacheMode

async def crawl_url(crawler, url, config):
    return await crawler.arun(url=url, config=config)

async def crawl_batch_manual():
    browser_conf = BrowserConfig(headless=True)
    run_conf = CrawlerRunConfig(
        cache_mode=CacheMode.BYPASS,
        stream=False,
        check_robots_txt=True,
    )

    urls = [
        "https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Main_Page",
        "https://news.ycombinator.com/",
        "https://crawl4ai.com/mkdocs/",
    ]

    async with AsyncWebCrawler(config=browser_conf) as crawler:
        tasks = [asyncio.create_task(crawl_url(crawler, u, run_conf)) for u in urls]
        results = await asyncio.gather(*tasks, return_exceptions=False)

    for url, result in zip(urls, results):
        if result.success:
            print(f"Success: {url}")
        else:
            print(f"Failed to crawl {url}: {result.error_message}")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(crawl_batch_manual())
```
